hook_text: Two sketches, one scorecard, no shouting. The ramp that wins is the one your own rules pick.
clip_script: Sketch two ideas that really differ: a straight ramp beside four steps, or a ramp that doubles back with a landing to fit half the length. Freehand, 3D, sizes written on. Then build a scorecard from your brief. Specifications first: 1 in 12, 1 200 wide, equal risers, landings, rails, kerb. Pass or fail, and a fail puts the idea out. Then considerations: fitness, safety, cost, ergonomics, looks, durability, environment, 1 to 5 with a reason in every cell. Score both ideas together, same card, same people. Add up. Say why in one sentence: B meets everything, 31 to 27, fits the site. Then fix B's weak rows, borrow A's best bit, and sketch the Final Idea.
visual_style: Whiteboard split screen of two ramp sketches; a grid scorecard filling with ticks, crosses and numbers; totals appearing; an arrow from the loser's stairs onto the winner.
pacing: Two ideas, the card, the scoring, the sentence, the development.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a five-row scorecard for choosing a phone.
